ETH at $2,725 (+0.2%) — the quote asset for most of these pools.
launches: 631 tokens launched in the last 7 days. 12 cleared the structural bar (liquidity, buyers, holders, concentration, no red flags). The three below ranked highest on the score; the rest of the passers are listed as "also passed".

1 of the 3 are under 12 hours old, which means every number on their card is launch-day data. Launch-day numbers are real but unstable: a token that looks like this at hour 3 often looks very different at hour 30.
Ticker clones are live on XDP (3 others) — check the contract address before buying anything with these names.
accumulation: Holder history exists for 54 tokens that are older than two days and traded today. The three below are adding wallets while price is flat, and the new holders are explained by unique buyers — airdrop spikes are filtered out.

This is the list a screener cannot give you. Someone is building a position without moving the chart. Whether that is smart money or a slow exit-liquidity trap is the research to do — the holder table and trade flow on page 2 are where to start.
fading: 105 tokens with real liquidity were checked for two or more fade signals at once: holders leaving, volume halving, sellers outnumbering buyers, a −25% day, or −40% from the 48h high.
Ranking is weighted by liquidity, so a fade on a token people actually hold outranks a fade on a $20k pool. If you hold one of these, the holder trend tends to show up before the chart does.
avoid: Only tokens with at least $3.0k of volume today — this is what people are actually buying, not a list of dead pools.
Most common failure: top-10 wallet concentration (3 of 6). A red flag here is a hard rule, not a judgement — the token is listed with the exact check it failed and the number behind it.
Combined, these 6 tokens did $325.65M of volume today. That is how much money went into tokens that fail a check you can run in one API call.
wallets: The top traders of the 14 most traded memes were pooled, and the 18 biggest realized-PnL wallets were checked wallet-wide.

6 sold tokens they never bought — team allocations, airdrops or transfers from another wallet — and 11 are bots or routers doing thousands of swaps. Neither is a trader you can copy, so they are dropped.
1 human-looking wallet remains. It made 80%+ of their PnL on a single token — one big hit, not a repeatable edge.
It holds under $5k on-chain right now: the money is out. Watch what they buy next, not what they bought last.
